Thanks again for the conversation today. As we start to plan the Hosted -> Dedicated swap for HelionAI, procurement asked for a concrete sizing validation and cutover plan we can include in the SOW. High-level asks from our side:

- A traffic model that shows expected GPU capacity at peak and steady state (we peaked last month at ~1.8M tokens/hour).
- Clear acceptance criteria for the canary and full rollout (latency targets, error budget, token variability).
- Recommended pre-warm windows and a dry-run plan.

I've attached a small CSV with our 30-day production trace (initial_traffic.csv) to help — note that ~12% of requests are >8k tokens due to batch summarization jobs.

Can you confirm what data points you need from our side and an initial timeline? Procurement is pushing for a decision by 2028-06-20.

Marco — thanks for the data, that helps a lot. Quick notes and requests so we can produce a sizing matrix:

1) Baseline assumptions we used to kick off analysis (please confirm):
   - Model: redwood-medium-7b (int8 optimized)
   - Average tokens per req: 650
   - Token distribution: 12% > 8k, 68% between 200-1200, 20% <200
   - Desired p95 server-side latency target: <= 200ms (generation only)
   - Safety factor: 1.5x for headroom during peak events

2) Data we still need from you:
   - % of traffic that can be scheduled for batch/async vs strictly low-latency path
   - Windows of traffic spikes (hour-of-day / day-of-week examples)

3) Initial validation outputs we'll provide next:
   - Traffic projection CSV (Q2->Q3) with GPU slot recommendation per timeframe
   - Acceptance matrix (p95/p99 latency, error-rate ceilings, KV cache hit assumptions)
   - Proposed dry-run timeline and pre-warm soak hours

I've attached our first-pass traffic projection (traffic_projection_q2_q3.csv) and will circulate a draft acceptance matrix once Aditya's team confirms capacity numbers. Can we aim for a pre-cutover dry-run the week of 2028-06-28? Procurement ETA of 06/20 is tight but workable if we lock the acceptance matrix this week.

Putting engineering numbers on the table — these are conservative recommendations based on the trace and the 12% >8k token tail: 

- Canary (step 0): 12 x A100-80GB (or 18 x A40 equiv) with 2-way redundancy for failover. Canary should cover ~10% expected production QPS with full tracing and metric collection.
- Staged steady state (step 1): 48 x A100-80GB for sustained throughput (assumes batching window 50ms, avg tokens 650). This maps to ~300 concurrent gen threads (model/shard config attached in the runbook stub).
- KV cache assumptions: warm cache + passive prefetching reduces token cost by ~18% in our sims. Plan a 72-hour warm soak before canary traffic.
- Long-context risk: anything above 12k tokens will trigger a different memory profile; if 12% of your traffic regularly runs >8k, we should plan a small fleet of long-context nodes (4 x 80GB) to isolate memory pressure.

Operational items for the runbook (will be in the acceptance matrix):
- Pre-warm window: 72 hours of synthetic traffic at 60% of projected peak to stabilize KV caches.
- Canary checks (automated): p95 latency, 5xx rate, token-per-request distribution, memory pressure per-gpu.
- Rollback condition: sustained p95 > 250ms for 15 minutes or error-rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes.

I'll export the shard mapping and a quick capacity table this afternoon and attach it to the acceptance matrix draft. If Helion can confirm the % of async/batched jobs, we can shrink the recommended steady-state by up to 20%.

-Aditya
Sr. Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
